summary.text: A 65-year-old woman with a longstanding history of hypertension and a mild cataract in both eyes noticed a sudden decrease in vision in her left eye, with no other ocular problems. Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/33 in the right eye and 6/100 in the left eye.

Fluorescein angiography showed a retinal arterial macroaneurysm with telangiectatic changes in the inferior temporal macular region, and OCT demonstrated subretinal hemorrhage extending into the foveal area with incomplete posterior vitreous detachment. Because of the submacular hemorrhage, some medicine was administered and she was followed up; the hemorrhage was absorbed 5 months later.

OCT then exhibited a full-thickness macular hole, 722 μm in diameter, with a macular epiretinal membrane. She was given a standard three-port pars plana vitrectomy with peeling of the internal limiting membrane and air filling of the vitreous cavity, with indocyanine green used and face-down positioning for a week afterward. Anatomic closure was achieved after 4 weeks and visual acuity improved to 15/100.
